# canvasplayer

> A browser player for Graffiti Markup Language (GML). It draws graffiti in 2D or 3D and provides embed examples. Public domain.

## Documentation

- [Getting started](https://github.com/jamiew/canvasplayer#install-and-use): Install and play a tag.
- [API](https://github.com/jamiew/canvasplayer#api): Modules, methods, events, and tag format.
- [Drawing options](https://github.com/jamiew/canvasplayer#drawing-options): Ink styles, effects, and data overlays.
- [WebGL](https://github.com/jamiew/canvasplayer#optional-webgl): Pass your own Three.js instance to ThreePlayer.
- [Embeds](https://jamiew.github.io/canvasplayer/embeds/): Animation, full player, and static drawing snippets.
- [Source](https://github.com/jamiew/canvasplayer): Code and tests.

## Basics

- No build step. The 2D player has no dependencies. WebGL needs Three.js as an optional peer.
- Pass a parsed tag to GmlPlayer or ThreePlayer. Pass a prepared tag to paint for a static drawing.
- gml.js handles data without a DOM or canvas. gml-ui.js provides controls for either renderer.
- Serve the files over HTTP or HTTPS. Browser modules do not load from file URLs.
- Call destroy when removing a player. Dispose of its controls too.
